subject: Commercial offer: renewal + 25% capacity uplift
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + capacity bump — initial commercial outline

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for the call last week. Based on your note about Q2 seasonality and keeping unit economics predictable, here9s a concise offer for BrightCart9s April renewal that we can move to DocuSign on once you confirm procurement routing: 

- Term: 12 months starting 2026-04-01
- Capacity: +25% committed baseline (effective at renewal)
- Commercial: 10% off list on the renewed committed baseline
- Credits: $50,000 onboarding credit to cover migration/validation work
- Price protection: 6-month price hold on per-token rates from go-live
- Burst treatment: blended overage model with a soft burst ceiling for quarter 1

I attached a one-page term summary with worked examples. If procurement prefers a longer hold or different credit structure, we9re open to trade-offs (longer hold vs. milestone-based credits). Please confirm the correct procurement contact (procurement@brightcart.com?) and whether legal will want any special wording in the order form.

Goal: align by Feb 25 so BrightCart can issue a PO in time for your Q2 planning. I9ll loop in Monica (CS) for the operational checklist once we9re agreed.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightcart.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity bump — initial commercial outline

Ben,

Appreciate the proposal. A few procurement/ops items from our side after internal review: 

1) Price hold: procurement9s vendor window review runs into Q3 — they9d prefer a 9-month hold rather than 6.
2) Credits: $50k looks helpful, but with our budget cadence we9d trade that for $35k up-front plus a smaller contingency payment (their preference is lower upfront cash).
3) Burst exposure: Ops wants a hard cap for the first 30 days after go-live to control risk. A per-token surcharge cap would be ideal instead of a blended rate.

I attached our usage export for Q4 2025 so you can see peak patterns. Procurement contact is procurement@brightcart.com and Alex Holt is the PO lead. Legal is on standby to review a near-final order form. We9re aiming to sign by Feb 26.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Head of Infrastructure & Data Platforms | BrightCart
samantha.lee@brightcart.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightcart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity bump — pricing trade-off proposal

Samantha,

Thanks for the detail and for sending the usage file. Quick commercial compromise to keep to your sign-off timeline: 

- Maintain a 6-month price hold as our standard protection window (we can discuss extensions with trade-offs).
- Rework credits to: $35,000 upfront onboarding credit + $15,000 milestone credit payable after production validation (total economic value = $50k but tied to success).
- Provide a hard 30-day burst surcharge cap at $0.034 per token beyond baseline (after 30 days, revert to blended overage model in the term sheet).

This minimizes Redwood9s short-term exposure while giving BrightCart a bounded go-live protection. If procurement requires 9 months, we could consider shifting part of the milestone into ongoing service credits (needs Marissa/finance approval).

If this works, I9ll update the term sheet and prepare DocuSign. Confirm: procurement contact Alex Holt and AR routing?

Ben
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: BrightCart renewal - commercial note

Forwarding Ben9s thread. Internal readout: procurement9s ask for 9 months of protection materially increases revenue exposure. Rough estimate: accepting 9 months instead of 6 could reduce year-1 NRR by ~USD 120k (depending on realized usage). Operational note: a longer hold exposes us to mid-year model/hardware cost moves, so any extension should be paired with stronger baseline commit or deferred milestone payments.

Recommendation: approve the $35k + $15k staged credit and the 30-day hard surcharge cap as Ben proposes. If finance pushes back on the $15k milestone, convert to service credit tied to onboarding tasks rather than cash.

Marissa
